comments.quote: And if the first question in a conversation is phrased in a way that draws a CDT answer, a later plain "what is the correct decision theory?" also gets CDT (18 of 20), with Claude explaining that it is staying consistent.

On concrete problems posed on their own (Newcomb, twin prisoner's dilemma, counterfactual mugging), the personas above did not change Claude's choices (one-box, cooperate, pay in 1,200 of 1,200 samples). But naming CDT earlier in the same conversation is a different matter: GPT-6 Astra, after naming CDT as its favorite under an academic cue, then two-boxes 58 of 58 times, defects against its twin 59 of 62 and refuses to pay the counterfactual mugger 62 of 62, against 0 of about 40 after naming FDT. The same experiment on Claude is still running.
